# Agent Memory Principles {.unnumbered}

Part I priced a bounded model call and asked when additional reasoning, candidates, or checks improve the selected result. Continuing a trajectory also requires deciding which information reaches the next call. In the repair task, the earlier failure trace describes one source version, the candidate patch changes that version, and the latest test covers only the conditions it exercised. Carrying all three forward without their relationships can mislead the next decision even when they fit in the context window. Part II addresses the State exposure of H·S·A by separating the selected context from its derived attention state and from information retained outside the session. Within a session ($S_1$), the runtime supplies working context and the serving system may retain reusable computation. Durable sources and records ($S_3$) outlive that session and must be retrieved to enter a later call. Task-local workspace artifacts ($S_2$) have their own execution and persistence requirements, developed in the following parts. These objects have different owners and validity conditions; they are not levels of one cache.

::: {#pri-vol3-attention-working-set .callout-principle title="Context is a selected working set"}

**Invariant**: A model's nominal context limit bounds the representation a call can admit, not the quality of decisions made from it. The runtime selects the next call's instructions, task state, observations, and retrieved material under that limit. Their usefulness depends on the task, model, arrangement, and quality criterion. The full treatment appears in @sec-vol3-context-engineering-physics.

**Implication**: Measure context policies on the intended workload and preserve output headroom when setting the input budget. Compaction must protect the exact fields the current task requires and distinguish information retained in the prompt from information available only through a later read. A shorter representation is useful only if the next decision remains adequate.

:::

What the runtime selects, the serving system must turn into attention state. Retaining that computation can reduce repeated work, but its validity differs from the relevance of the information it encodes.

::: {#pri-vol3-prefix-coherence .callout-principle title="Attention state is derived from the token prefix"}

**Invariant**: For the causal full-attention decoder considered here, reusable key-value state depends on the exact preceding token sequence and compatible model inputs and configuration, including positions and attention masks. A changed token prevents ordinary prefix reuse from that position onward. Matching tokens permit reuse only when compatible cached state remains available. The full treatment appears in @sec-vol3-kvcache-radix-tree.

**Implication**: Keep stable material ahead of frequently changing material where the request format and task permit, without preserving obsolete information merely to retain a cache hit. The serving system can share, retain, offload, or recompute derived state according to resource costs. Losing cached tensors loses reusable computation rather than task knowledge when the inputs and configuration needed to reconstruct them remain available.

:::

Information that must outlive a session belongs in an external store. Returning a record to the model requires selecting it and supplying its contents, not merely retaining its location.

::: {#pri-vol3-retrieval-contract .callout-principle title="Retrieval is a contract, not recall"}

**Invariant**: Durable information re-enters the model only when it is retrieved and staged into context. A retrieval score ranks candidates under a search rule; it does not establish that a record is current, authoritative for the claim, or permitted for this task. The full treatment appears in @sec-vol3-persistent-governance.

**Implication**: Every read from durable storage, whether the runtime pre-stages it or the model requests it through a search tool, needs a contract that bounds access, returned content, resource use, and the required freshness. The runtime chooses the retrieval method by the information need and checks the provenance and applicability of returned candidates before using them as evidence.

:::

The same record can remain useful as history while losing support for a claim about the current environment. Managing that distinction requires identifying which source and conditions a claim depends on.

::: {#pri-vol3-source-authority .callout-principle title="Authority stays with the source"}

**Invariant**: A staged excerpt, summary, or retrieval index does not supersede the designated source for the claim it represents. An observation describes the source version and conditions under which it was obtained. A later relevant change can invalidate its use as evidence about the present without making the historical observation false. Source provenance does not itself grant action permission or establish task acceptance. The full treatment appears in @sec-vol3-context-engineering-context-rot for the prompt and in @sec-vol3-persistent-invalidation for durable stores.

**Implication**: Track the dependencies of current claims and reconsider affected views when their relevant sources or conditions change. Refresh, remove, or explicitly mark unsupported current-state claims while retaining historical evidence when needed. Version checks help identify changed artifacts; age limits can trigger a refresh but do not prove freshness, and an unrelated write need not invalidate every retained observation.

:::

@Sec-vol3-context-engineering decides which information each call sees and how to keep that working context bounded and applicable. @Sec-vol3-kv-cache follows the selected tokens into the serving system and prices holding their attention state across turns, forks, and tool waits. @Sec-vol3-long-term-memory decides what outlives the session and how stored information returns to a task. Selecting useful information still supplies no permission to act on it; Part III develops the tool and execution boundaries through which proposals can affect the environment.
